content.introduction: According to Goldman Sachs, the S&P 500 is projected to rally more than expected, rising 6% to 6,600 in the next six months and 11% to 6,900 in the next 12 months, up from previous forecasts of 6,100 and 6,500 respectively. This change is attributed to earlier and deeper rate cuts from the Federal Reserve, lower bond yields, continued strength in large stocks, and investors' tolerance for near-term earnings weakness. Meanwhile, the Wall Street Courier's analysis indicates robust mid-term trend conditions with a bullish WSC Mid-Term Price Trend and a 91.3% probability of remaining in Risk-Off territory over the next five trading days. The Markets.com forecast suggests a 7,800–8,100 base range for the end of 2026, with earnings growth supportive but subject to changes in valuations, inflation, Treasury yields, Federal Reserve policy, and megacap leadership.

Mid-term TREND conditions remain robust, holding at their maximum reading. The WSC Trend Index continues to indicate broad-based strength, with a high percentage of stocks trading above their 52-week highs. The WSC Mid-Term Price Trend remains bullish, and the market closed above its 100-day moving average, with the EMA 100 Line still rising. Participation metrics such as the Percentage of Stocks Above 100-Day MA and 150-Day MA both confirm that the majority of index constituents are in [...] The current combination of Short-Term and Mid-Term Market Health situates the regime as very stable, with a 91.3% probability of remaining in Risk-Off territory over the next five trading days (Increasing Risk 89.1%, High Risk 2.2%). [...] The regime flipped from Risk-On (Very High Reward) to Risk-Off (Increasing Risk) today, ending a one-day run of the prior regime.
 Tomorrow's regime-retention probability is 91%, with an 89% chance of remaining in Increasing Risk; five-day regime change probability stands at 39%.
 Seven indicators flipped today, three in Trend, three in Trend Quality, and one in Sentiment, while all dimensions saw activity.

This S&P 500 Forecast uses a 7,800–8,100 base range for the end of 2026, balanced against meaningful bear and bull scenarios. Earnings growth remains supportive, but valuations, inflation, Treasury yields, Federal Reserve policy and narrow megacap leadership can change the outlook quickly. The 2027 and 2030 ranges are wider because each additional year introduces more uncertainty. Technical levels can help traders monitor the near-term trend, but they do not guarantee future prices. US stocks may rally more than previously forecast as the Federal Reserve is projected to cut rates earlier than expected, according to Goldman Sachs Research.

The S&P 500 Index is forecast to rise 6% to 6,600 (up from a previous forecast of 6,100) in the next six months and 11% to 6,900 (up from 6,500) in the next 12 months, David Kostin, chief US equity strategist in Goldman Sachs Research, writes in the team’s report dated July 7. [...] The forecast change reflects our economists’ projections of earlier and deeper rate easing from the Fed and projections for lower bond yields, continued strength in the largest stocks, and investors’ willingness to tolerate likely near-term weakness in company earnings. [...] Shifting trade policy creates significant uncertainty around company earnings forecasts. Kostin’s team maintained its projection for the growth in S&P 500 stocks’ earnings-per-share at 7% in 2025 and 7% the following year.
